characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: step size of 1 μm, 300 nm, 100 nm and 30 nm

characterization_methods.purpose: determine phase fractions and austenite stability after tensile deformation

characterization_methods.technique: electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) and wet-chemical analysis

analytical_models.equation_role: γ_SFE = 2ρΔG^{γ→ε} + 2σ links stacking fault energy to the γ→ε molar Gibbs energy
analytical_models.model_note: Fe-Mn-Al-C Gibbs energy expression (Eq. 4) with magnetic term (Eqs. 5–8).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: test temperature T = 293 K (RT) or 77 K (LNT)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: well-accepted thermodynamic approach (Eqs. 3–8) using literature parameters
computational_details.simulation_method: thermodynamic calculation of stacking fault energy (SFE) and γ→ε Gibbs energy
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: SFE 62.64 mJ·m⁻² (RT) is higher than the 20–45 mJ·m⁻² range where deformation twinning is expected, yet twinning is observed experimentally — a controversy discussed in the paper.
Calculated diagram shows a small BCC (ferrite) fraction at the solution-treatment temperature, consistent with the ~3 vol.% α observed experimentally and with the stability of the two phases.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: u = EBSD unit length; b = Burgers vector; θ = average KAM value of the selected area
computational_details.simulation_method: geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density estimation from EBSD KAM
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: GND densities rise from 0.71 to 8.99 × 10^14 m^-2 for RT deformation.

analytical_models.model_note: D = average crystallite size; ⟨ε²⟩^{1/2} = average micro-strain.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: profiles of (111)_γ, (200) and (220) diffraction peaks after Gaussian fitting; b = 0.26 nm
computational_details.simulation_method: dislocation density estimation from XRD peak broadening (Williamson-Hall)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Total dislocation density ρ (RT-XRD) increases from 0.64 to 8.03 × 10^14 m^-2 with RT strain, consistent with the GND trend.

computational_details.simulation_method: critical twinning stress estimation (mean-field and Hall-Petch-type models)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Experimental critical twinning stress at RT (~723 MPa) is far smaller than the estimates (939/1153/1306/1096 MPa at RT); at LNT the experimental value (778 MPa) approaches the Sachs-model prediction.

analytical_models.equation_role: σ_dis(γ or α) = M α G b ρ^0.5
analytical_models.model_note: σ_diff verified against α = 0.136, 0.26, 0.4 at 10 % and 20 % RT strain (Table 7).
RT twin strengthening is negligible (only σ_twin appears at 55 % LNT = 290 MPa).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: φ_ferrite ≈ 3 % (neglected in final calculation); austenite parameters M = 3.06, α = 0.4, G = 68 GPa, b = 0.26 nm; ferrite M = 2.8, α = 0.2, G = 80.7 GPa, b = 0.248 nm
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated dislocation (σ_dis) and twin (σ_twin) contributions agree well with measured flow stress at RT (Fig. 13a); α = 0.4 gives the smallest σ_diff (15 and 25 MPa at 10 % and 20 % RT strain).

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Deformation twin boundaries act as effective barriers to dislocation motion, reducing the dislocation mean free path (dynamic Hall-Petch effect); at RT this contributes only at the highest strains as very few twins form.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: stress concentration at cell-block walls (planar slip)
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Type II and III grains form cell block walls with planar-slip characteristics that create the stress concentration required for twinning nucleation/growth, whereas type I grains form uniform dislocation cells that disperse macroscopic shear stress.

interfaces.interface_notes: Deformation twinning at RT is first observed after ~28 % tensile strain and remains of very low fraction up to 38 %; twinning occurs preferentially in type II and type III grains oriented away from <100>//TA.
interfaces.phase_evolution: No phase transformation occurs during RT tensile deformation; the austenite (γ) fraction stays essentially constant (~97 %) and the ~3 vol.% BCC α ferrite is stable, even after large tensile strain.

phase_interfaces.coherence: FCC/BCC interfaces are incoherent; in duplex low-density steels the main crack sources originate from the FCC/BCC interfaces

interfaces.slip_behavior: At RT the early stage of deformation favours dislocation slip over twinning (the average {111}<110>_γ Schmid factor reaches its maximum near 3 % tensile strain, while the average {111}<112>_γ Schmid factor decreases at that strain). Planar slip dominates, with single glide traces in type II grains, double glide traces in type III grains and few slip traces in type I grains; type I grains form dislocation cells while type II and III grains form cell blocks.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 50 kg ingot with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-6Al-0.1C-0.1Nb-0.1V-1Mo-1W (wt.%) prepared by vacuum induction melting.
As-cast ingot homogenized at 1150 °C for 4 h.
Subsequently hot-rolled (HR) into rods with a diameter of 16.5 mm.
HR rods solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by oil quenching to obtain equiaxed grain structures (parent process proc_st-1050c-2h-oq shared by both RT and LNT states).

Tensile tests on standard specimens (gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, tensile axis parallel to rod axis) at an initial strain rate of 1.0 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ at room temperature using an MTS machine; interrupted tests to engineering strains of 3 %, 10 %, 20 %, 28 %, 38 % and 55 %; at least three specimens deformed to fracture.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: MTS tensile machine; at least three specimens deformed until fracture to confirm reproducibility; interrupted tests to engineering strains of 3 %, 10 %, 20 %, 28 %, 38 % and 55 %
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard tensile specimens, gauge length 25 mm and diameter 5 mm, tensile axis parallel to the rod axis

strain_hardening_rate: RT strain hardening curve divided into two stages (stage markers A and A'); RT hardening rate descends from about 2500 MPa; RT hardening behaviour governed mainly by dislocation substructure refinement
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: RT engineering stress-strain curve (Fig. 2a) and RT true stress-strain curve (Fig. 2b); RT curve yields near 250 MPa and peaks just under 600 MPa with failure around engineering strain 0.52

grain_structure.texture: very weak texture along the forging direction

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with many annealing twin boundaries (white lines)
small particles uniformly distributed along the austenite grain boundaries

precipitates.type: MC carbide (containing Nb, Mo, W; V fully dissolved)

structures.overall_structure: Equiaxed FCC γ-austenite matrix embedded with a small fraction of BCC α ferrite uniformly distributed along the austenite grain boundaries; many annealing twin boundaries; very weak texture; L1₂-type short-range order and faint superlattice/satellite reflections; MC carbide present.

structures.microstructure_counts: 5 interrupted strain states examined at RT (3, 10, 20, 28, 38 % engineering strain)

defects.type: complex dislocation configurations: dislocation nodes, multiple dislocations and dislocation pairs (planar slip)
Lomer-Cottrell (LC) locks and high-density dislocation walls (HDDWs)
Taylor lattices, cell blocks (CBs) and dislocation cells (DCs) along {111} slip planes; type I grains form dislocation cells, type II/III grains form cell blocks
refined cell blocks and dislocation cells; a small amount of deformation twinning formed along cell block walls (CBWs); a few microbands (stress localization)
deformation twins parallel to the primary slip plane further developed but proportion still very low; cell blocks and twins

grain_structure.texture: strong <111>//TA texture and weak <100>//TA texture developed at RT

structures.number_of_phases: 2 (γ austenite + α ferrite) with no phase transformation during RT deformation
structures.overall_structure: RT tensile deformation is controlled by planar dislocation slip and dislocation substructure refinement (Taylor lattices → cell blocks (CBs) and dislocation cells (DCs) → refinement) with a small amount of deformation twinning appearing only just before necking (~28 % strain). No phase transformation occurs in the austenite.

unmapped_findings: CVN (Charpy V-notch) impact energy at RT is 331 ± 4 J (Table 2) — measured by Charpy V-notch impact test on separate standard impact specimens (55 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm, V-notch depth 2 mm), not on the RT tensile specimen itself.
Instrumented Charpy impact at RT: crack initiation energy Wm = 79.28 J and crack propagation energy Wp = 251.33 J (Fig. 2c); total impact energy at RT is governed by crack propagation energy.
Reduction of area at RT is 78 ± 0.5 % (Table 2).

True stress of the RT tensile specimen (Table 3): 339 MPa at 3.0 % engineering strain (3.0 % true strain), 483 MPa at 10.0 % (9.5 % true), 635 MPa at 20.0 % (18.2 % true), 723 MPa at 28.0 % (24.7 % true) and 800 MPa at 38.0 % (32.2 % true); not measured at 55 %.
Lattice friction stress of the austenite at RT is 143 MPa (calculated by Eq. 16 from the RT yield strength minus grain-boundary strengthening).

Experimental critical twinning stress at RT is about 723 MPa (Table 5), far smaller than the model estimates of 939 MPa (M = 2.2), 1153 MPa (M = 2.7), 1306 MPa (M = 3.06) and 1096 MPa (Hall-Petch-type relation).
At RT, deformation twinning is first observed after about 28 % tensile strain (a small fraction along cell-block walls), confirming that RT twinning occurs only just before necking.
Hardness is not reported for the RT tensile specimen (no hardness testing was performed).
